short: The client tier: one workspace, two packages
is: The client tier — one yarn workspace of two packages: `web`, the SvelteKit app fronting the axum backend, and `ui`, the `@zurfur/ui` component library with its gallery. This directory holds the workspace root, its one lockfile and the install guard.
conventions: Plain SvelteKit + TypeScript — the Leptos and ZesTTY/Dialect alternatives were both retired 2026-08-09; don't re-litigate the stack without new evidence.
The React auth frontend is deleted.

Every install is the trio `node frontend/install-check.mjs`, `yarn --cwd frontend install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, `node frontend/install-check.mjs --installed`: `just frontend-install` locally, the same three steps in CI's `ui`, `web` and `contract` jobs; `scripts/tools-check.sh` fails a workflow that installs any other way.

`web` takes `@zurfur/ui` as a dev dependency at exactly `0.0.0`, resolved by the workspace symlink; `.npmrc` points the `@zurfur` scope at `registry.invalid`, so the package can never be fetched from npm.

A change to `yarn.lock` or `lexicons/package-lock.json` is checked by CI's `npm-lock` job (scripts/npm-lock-ci.sh): `lock-review.mjs --licences --min-age-days 7` with the base's npm-licences.json and waivers, and osv-scanner; a change that edits npm-licences.json has both lockfiles swept against it by the base's `lock-review.mjs --licence-sweep`; locally, `just npm-lock-review <rev>` runs the same floor and licence rule (needs the network).

fs.name: .npmrc
fs.role: engine-strict=true, so the declared node/yarn range is enforced on install, and the @zurfur scope pointed at registry.invalid so @zurfur/ui can never be fetched from npm; the guard pins these two lines

fs.name: install-check.mjs
fs.role: the install guard, Node built-ins only: before install it pins the workspace's shape (root keys, the workspaces list, no .yarnrc, one .npmrc with its two lines), refuses yarn rc files in /etc, the home folder, yarn's config folder and every folder above the repo root, and any YARN_* or npm_config_* variable (named, never its value), refuses any spec that is not a plain range and any workspace range missing from the lockfile (yarn 1's --frozen-lockfile doesn't check workspace dependencies), and holds every lockfile block to what yarn writes: one package per block, only version, resolved, integrity, dependencies and optionalDependencies, every key and dependency range a plain range in the shapes the guard reads (*, X.Y.Z, =X.Y.Z, ^X.Y.Z, ~X.Y.Z, ^X, joined by ||), a version that satisfies each of its keys (yarn drops an entry that doesn't and resolves the range unlocked), resolved exactly that package's registry tarball with its sha1, sha512 integrity, no duplicate keys, and every dependency a block lists itself a lockfile key (yarn resolves a missing one from the registry, unlocked); with --installed it refuses install scripts and binding.gyp off an empty allow list and requires @zurfur/ui to be a symlink to ui/

fs.name: install-check.test.mjs
fs.role: the guard's node:test fixtures (run with node --test, in just gate, gate-light and CI's ui job)

fs.name: licences.mjs
fs.role: the licence rule: the SPDX expression parser, the strict loader of npm-licences.json and the verdict on one package version (bundled code fails, then an exception may admit it, then the licence must be readable and allowed by the list), plus the npm naming rule lock-review.mjs re-exports; pure, Node built-ins and install-check.mjs only

fs.name: licences.test.mjs
fs.role: the licence rule's node:test fixtures, offline with a fixed date (run with node --test, in just gate, gate-light and CI's ui job)

fs.name: lock-review.mjs
fs.role: the npm lockfiles' review against the registry (it needs the network), in two modes. The review of a change, which CI's npm-lock job runs as the base commit's copy through scripts/npm-lock-ci.sh and `just npm-lock-review <rev>` runs locally: reads two yarn v1 or two npm lockfileVersion 3 files (a v3 link or bundled entry, one without integrity or resolved outside registry.npmjs.org is refused), lists the entries a change removed and added (an npm entry newly installed under an alias counts as added), and checks each added entry against its full registry document, fetched once with no redirects: the integrity must match; with --licences <file> the licence must pass the list (licences.mjs) and a package the list scopes must not be installed under an alias; with --min-age-days N (which needs --licences) the version must be at least N days old unless --waivers names that exact name@version (a waiver lifts only the age finding). The sweep, `--licence-sweep --licences <file> <lockfile>…`, which `just npm-licences` (in `just gate`), the daily advisories job and CI's npm-lock job (when a change edits the list) run: checks every entry of each lockfile, once per (name, version, integrity), against its per-version registry document (its own name, version and integrity must match), the list and the alias rule, prints a count per licence and notes each exception no entry used. Names, versions, the documents, the waiver file and the list are read fail-closed; the registry lookups and the clock are injected only through main(), never the environment; exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 errors

fs.name: lock-review.test.mjs
fs.role: lock-review's node:test fixtures, offline through the injected lookups and clock: the age floor, waivers and the waiver file, the licence rule and the sweep (aliases in both formats, bundles, exceptions, the per-version document, the counts) over fixture lists and the real npm-licences.json, fail-closed registry reads, the npm v3 reader, the CLI's exit codes, that each frontend tool on scripts/npm-lock-ci.sh's TOOLS line imports nothing outside that set, and the naming rule and v3 reader over the real lockfiles

fs.name: package.json
fs.role: the workspace root, exactly {"private": true, "workspaces": ["web", "ui"]}; the guard pins it

fs.name: ui/
fs.role: @zurfur/ui: the component library and its gallery

fs.name: yarn.lock
fs.role: the one lockfile for both packages; yarn is the package manager

notes: See also: ZMVP-148 (the deleted React auth frontend).
The install guard does not check .npmrc files outside the repo (in $HOME, /etc or above the repo root); CI runners have a clean home.
